title: End the drain cleanly when a landing adds a config key it can't parse
summary: When a landed job's athena.toml diff adds a key the running binary's schema rejects, the drain should keep the job recorded as landed and end the run with a "reinstall" note instead of Stop::RepeatedFailure. Audience: the person running `athena drain`, who today sees a false 'repeated failure' for a job that landed.

defaults_applied.how: Change and test are in Rust.
Criteria require cargo test, clippy and fmt to pass with a new test.
Criteria check the landed-not-failed record and the reinstall stop by running a test.
Distinguish the unknown-key-from-newer-build condition rather than suppressing failures generally.
One focused change to drain stop handling plus a changelog entry.
Behavior criteria use commands the verifier can run.
The check is the user-visible stop reason and the job's landed record.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs (Stop enum ~l.794, land ~l.1408, work-item attempt loop ~l.1470-1527 where ATTEMPTS failures give ItemEnd::Failed, finish ~l.1977 mapping ItemEnd::Failed to Stop::RepeatedFailure, rebuild_if_due ~l.1951, Steps::land ~l.3078), crates/athena-core/src/capability.rs (JobConfig::at calls Config::parse, which fails on unknown keys as crates/athena-data/src/config.rs uses deny_unknown_fields) and crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs (dispatch calls JobConfig::at at l.707). Entry point is the drain loop; after a landing the next config read at the new head fails and the error currently counts as a job failure.
The 'drain code' is crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs (and display.rs/main.rs help text for the new stop reason), which the request's scope includes alongside crates/athena-core/src/run/.

The fix adds a distinguishable condition (for example a typed error from the config parse of a landed commit, or a check that the job is already landed) and a new Stop variant (for example Stop::Reinstall) with label, meaning and a note telling the user to reinstall (setup.sh). The landed job's record stays landed and it is not counted as failed. Exact naming is the producer's choice.

The drain's existing tests drive the loop through a stub Steps; the new test lives in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs or drain.rs's unit tests, and may also use run/tests.rs for the core piece. Stop::ALL tests (all variants have labels and meanings) must be kept passing.

No record or data file is added under crates/, so the records allow-list is untouched. No refusal rule is added or tightened, so no refusal-rate criterion applies. Governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml) are not changed; the test builds its own key in a test repository.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test in the drain tests lands a job whose diff adds a key to athena.toml that the running Config schema does not know; `cargo test -p athena-cli drain` passes and the test asserts the job's landing is recorded as landed (not failed) and the report's stop is the new reinstall stop, not Stop::RepeatedFailure.
The same test asserts the run's output/report text includes a note telling the user to reinstall, and does not contain 'repeated failure'; run with `cargo test -p athena-cli`.

A genuine second failure of the same item (no landing) still ends with Stop::RepeatedFailure; the existing test asserting 'repeated failure: item a failed twice' in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs still passes under `cargo test`.

Changes are confined to crates/athena-core/src/run/, the drain code in crates/athena-cli/src/ (drain.rs, plus display.rs/main.rs text for the new stop), their tests, and CHANGELOG.md; git diff shows no other paths.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing that the drain now ends the run with a reinstall note, not a repeated failure, when a landing adds a config key the running build cannot parse.

The module docs in drain.rs and the Stop meaning text describe the new stop reason; the unknown-key condition is distinguished from other config errors (an unparsable config not caused by a newer landed build is still a failure).
`cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes (tested default).

out_of_scope: Making the config parser tolerant of unknown keys in general
Automatically reinstalling or rebuilding the binary on this condition
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower pass chance than reference: the failure path spans core config parsing and the drain's stop logic in another crate, and the exact failing point is unconfirmed.
hard_reason: This changes the drain's stop rules and how a job's failure is recorded, which is the run pipeline and its drain.
